answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost. A sonnet stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a lantern holds the rep...
